messages:
acme_admin: Hey, onboarding help — we invited a contractor and they accepted, but when they switch to the project in the console all action buttons are greyed out and API calls return 403.
acme_admin: They show up in Members with role "Viewer" at org level, but we expected project-level write access.
acme_admin: Repro: login -> switch org -> open Project "Project Orion" -> attempt to create deployment -> get 403 JSON: {"error":"permission_denied","reason":"missing_project_role"} 
acme_admin: This was an invite flow today (SCIM off). Any quick checks?
maria_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact invite flow? Was the user added via email invite or SSO group?
acme_admin: Email invite through console. They clicked the magic link and accepted. No SCIM or group sync.
maria_support: Thanks. Two quick things: (1) browser session caching can show the project in the list but not the refreshed role set; (2) API keys created before role propagation can be scoped to old membership.
maria_support: Can you ask the user to hard-refresh or log out and back in? Also try creating a new API key from their profile and retry.
olivia_se: If they accepted and still only have org Viewer, looks like project-level binding never applied. Did you add them as a collaborator on the project or rely on an inherited role?
acme_admin: We added them as a Project Member in the project settings after they accepted — screenshots attached in thread. Buttons still disabled.
dan_prod: Hi — I looked up the project. We recently toggled the new "restrict-project-actions" feature for that project (opt-in). If that flag is on, org-level roles are intentionally not promoted to project-level for onboarded users until an additional approval step. Could that be it?
acme_admin: Oh — yes that project was set to restricted during setup. Didn't realize that would block existing invites.
maria_support: That matches the 403 reason. Quick workaround: add them explicitly as Project Editor (or Admin) in the project settings for now. We'll continue with root-cause.
acme_admin: Workaround worked — they can create deployments now. Would like to understand fix so future invites don't hit this.
dan_prod: I'll open a config check — likely the onboarding flow didn't surface the approval step when the feature flag was enabled. If we confirm, we'll route the flow to request project approval during acceptance.
dan_prod: For audit: can you paste the user's display email and the invite ts? I'll attach the logs.
acme_admin: user: contractor+orion@acme.com, invite_ts: 4105556601
sre_bot: [audit] invite/accept event: user=contractor+orion@acme.com, project=proj_7f8b, invite_ts=4105556601, accept_ts=4105556690, role_assigned=org_viewer, project_binding_attempt=skipped_restricted_flag
maria_support: Thanks — that confirms. I'll escalate to product for UX change and to engineering to ensure acceptance flow returns explicit error/notice instead of silently showing the project without actions.
maria_support: In the meantime, recommended steps for customers: 1) If you use restricted-projects, add necessary users explicitly as project members during onboarding. 2) If someone reports greyed buttons, try a forced logout + new API key.
acme_admin: Appreciate the quick help. Please keep me posted on the product ticket ID.
dan_prod: Filed ENG ticket INF-9982 (onboarding visibility + restricted flag) and linked audit log. Will update when we have a permanent fix.
maria_support: Closing the support thread for now since workaround applied. Reopen if anything else breaks. :thumbsup:
